proof_ideas.proof_excerpt:
by
  have hne1 : ((1 + δ : ℝ) : ℂ) ≠ 1 := by
    intro h
    have := congrArg Complex.re h
    simp at this
    linarith
  have hrw : DirichletCharacter.LFunction (1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ N) ((1 + δ : ℝ) : ℂ)
      = DirichletCharacter.LFunctionTrivChar N ((1 + δ : ℝ) : ℂ) := rfl
  rw [hrw, DirichletCharacter.LFunctionTrivChar_eq_mul_riemannZeta hne1, norm_mul]
  have hprod : ‖∏ p ∈ N.primeFactors, (1 - (p : ℂ) ^ (-((1 + δ : ℝ) : ℂ)))‖ ≤ 1 := by
    rw [norm_prod]
    refine Finset.prod_le_one (fun p _ => norm_nonneg _) (fun p hp => ?_)
    have hp0 : (0 : ℝ) < p := by
      exact_mod_cast (Nat.prime_of_mem_primeFactors hp).pos
    have hcpow : (p : ℂ) ^ (-((1 + δ : ℝ) : ℂ)) = (((p : ℝ) ^ (-(1 + δ)) : ℝ) : ℂ) := by
      rw [Complex.ofReal_cpow hp0.le]
      push_cast
      rfl
    rw [hcpow]
    have hr0 : 0 ≤ (p : ℝ) ^ (-(1 + δ)) := Real.rpow_nonneg hp0.le _
    have hr1 : (p : ℝ) ^ (-(1 + δ)) ≤ 1 := by
      have hp1 : (1 : ℝ) ≤ p := by exact_mod_cast (Nat.prime_of_mem_primeFactors hp).one_le
      exact Real.rpow_le_one_of_one_le_of_nonpos hp1 (by linarith)
    rw [show (1 : ℂ) - (((p : ℝ) ^ (-(1 + δ)) : ℝ) : ℂ) = ((1 - (p : ℝ) ^ (-(1 + δ)) : ℝ) : ℂ) by
      push_cast; ring, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_of_nonneg (by linarith)]
    linarith
  have hzeta : ‖riemannZeta ((1 + δ : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ ≤ 1 / δ + 2 := by
    have h := abs_riemannZeta_one_add_le hδ
    have hcast : ((1 + δ : ℝ) : ℂ) = (1 : ℂ) + (δ : ℂ) := by push_cast; ring
    rw [hcast]
    exact h
  calc ‖∏ p ∈ N.primeFactors, (1 - (p : ℂ) ^ (-((1 + δ : ℝ) : ℂ)))‖
        * ‖riemannZeta ((1 + δ : ℝ) : ℂ)‖
      ≤ 1 * (1 / δ + 2) := by
        apply mul_le_mul hprod hzeta (norm_nonneg _) (by norm_num)
    _ = 1 / δ + 2 := one_mul _

theorem primeDirichletNaturalOccupationProduct_eq
    (sigma t : ℝ) (ν : ℕ →₀ ℕ) :
    ν.prod (fun n k =>
        primeDirichletEulerCoefficient sigma t (natEquivPrimes n) ^ k) =
      primeWavePhase t (primeProduct ((Finsupp.domCongr natEquivPrimes) ν)) *

by
  classical
  let A : ℂ := ((-sigma : ℝ) : ℂ) - (t : ℂ) * Complex.I
  let κ : Nat.Primes →₀ ℕ := (Finsupp.domCongr natEquivPrimes) ν
  have hlog : Real.log (primeProduct κ : ℝ) =
      ν.sum fun n k => (k : ℝ) * Real.log (natEquivPrimes n : ℕ) := by
    rw [log_primeProduct]
    simp [κ, Finsupp.sum, Finsupp.domCongr_apply, Finsupp.equivMapDomain]
  have hprod :
      ν.prod (fun n k =>
          primeDirichletEulerCoefficient sigma t (natEquivPrimes n) ^ k) =
        Complex.exp (A * (Real.log (primeProduct κ : ℝ) : ℂ)) := by
    rw [Finsupp.prod]
    calc
      ∏ n ∈ ν.support,
          primeDirichletEulerCoefficient sigma t (natEquivPrimes n) ^ ν n =
          ∏ n ∈ ν.support,
            Complex.exp ((ν n : ℂ) *
              (A * (Real.log (natEquivPrimes n : ℕ) : ℂ))) := by
        apply Finset.prod_congr rfl
        intro n _
        rw [primeDirichletEulerCoefficient_eq_exp]
        change Complex.exp (A * (Real.log (natEquivPrimes n : ℕ) : ℂ)) ^ ν n = _
        exact (Complex.exp_nat_mul
          (A * (Real.log (natEquivPrimes n : ℕ) : ℂ)) (ν n)).symm
      _ = Complex.exp (∑ n ∈ ν.support,
            ((ν n : ℂ) *
              (A * (Real.log (natEquivPrimes n : ℕ) : ℂ)))) := by
        exact (Complex.exp_sum ν.support fun n =>
          ((ν n : ℂ) *
            (A * (Real.log (natEquivPrimes n : ℕ) : ℂ)))).symm
      _ = Complex.exp (A * (Real.log (primeProduct κ : ℝ) : ℂ)) := by
        congr 1
        rw [hlog]
        change (∑ n ∈ ν.support, (ν n : ℂ) *
            (A * (Real.log (natEquivPrimes n : ℕ) : ℂ))) =
          A * (((∑ n ∈ ν.support,
            (ν n : ℝ) * Real.log (natEquivPrimes n : ℕ)) : ℝ) : ℂ)
        push_cast
        rw [Finset.mul_sum]
        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
        intro n _
        ring
  rw [hprod]
  have hκpos : 0 < primeProduct κ := primeProduct_pos κ
  rw [primeWavePhase, if_neg hκpos.ne', Real.rpow_def_of_pos (by exact_mod_cast hκpos)]
  change Complex.exp (A * (Real.log (primeProduct κ : ℝ) : ℂ)) =
    Complex.exp (-(((t * Real.log (primeProduct κ : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)) *
      ((Real.exp (Real.log (primeProduct κ : ℝ) * -sigma) : ℝ) : ℂ)

## 0. Why this object

Two corpus results fix the direction.

1. `euler-defect-controls-displacement.md` **falsified** every attempt to control zero displacement
   by an *analytic size* measure of non-multiplicativity: displacement responds to a coefficient
   perturbation like `1/|L'(rho)|`, which is unbounded, so no norm on the coefficients that is
   continuous under `L ↦ L + eps·g` can work. Its successor statement: *any proof of
   "Euler product ⟹ RH" must use a feature of multiplicativity that is **discontinuous** in the
   coefficients.* It named the candidate — discreteness of the value set of the coefficients of
   `-L'/L` — and left as the immediate finite task: *construct or exclude a non-multiplicative `L`
   with a zeta-type functional equation and discrete `b_n`.*
2. `downstream-functionals-of-the-zero-set.md` forbids any further `RH ⟺ X`.

This card supplies the exact discrete invariant, prime by prime, and reduces the finite task to a
finite algebraic condition. Nothing here is a functional of the zero set; everything is a statement
about the coefficient sequence, which is what *produces* the zeros.

**Parent theory used.** `[LITERATURE]` Kaczorowski–Perelli, *On the structure of the Selberg class,
I: 0 ≤ d ≤ 1*, Acta Math. **182** (1999), 207–241: every element of the **extended** Selberg class
`S^#` of degree one is, up to a single vertical shift `s ↦ s + i·theta` forced by the imaginary part
of the gamma-factor parameter `mu`, a Dirichlet series with **periodic** coefficients

  `F(s) = sum_{n>=1} alpha(n) n^{-s-i theta}`,  `alpha` periodic mod `q`,  `alpha(1) = 1`,

and the functional equation is exactly the statement that the vector `alpha` is an eigenvector of
the finite Fourier transform on `Z/q` (a Gauss-sum condition; Dirichlet characters are the
eigenvectors coming from Euler products, Davenport–Heilbronn mod 5 is an eigenvector that is not).
`[LITERATURE]` Saias–Weingartner: a periodic Dirichlet series that is not `P(s)L(s,chi)` has
infinitely many zeros in `sigma > 1`; so in degree one "no zeros right of 1" already **is** the
Euler product. The open question is the analogous statement at `1/2`.

---

## 1. The virtual local polynomial

Fix `F` as above with `theta = 0` for the moment, `alpha` periodic mod `q`, `alpha(1)=1`. Write

  `log F(s) = sum_{n>=2} c_n n^{-s}`,  `-F'/F(s) = sum_{n>=2} b_n n^{-s}`,  `b_n = c_n log n`.

Because a factorisation of `p^m` uses only powers of `p`, the coefficient `c_{p^m}` depends only on
the *local* data `(alpha(p^i))_{i>=0}`. For `p` coprime to `q` with `d = ord_q(p)` the sequence
`i ↦ alpha(p^i)` is `d`-periodic, so its generating function is rational:

  `G_p(X) = sum_{i>=0} alpha(p^i) X^i = N_p(X) / (1 - X^d)`,
  **`N_p(X) := sum_{i=0}^{d-1} alpha(p^i) X^i`,  `N_p(0) = 1`.**

`N_p` is the **virtual local polynomial** of `F` at `p`. If `F` has an Euler product then
`G_p(X) = 1/(1 - alpha(p) X)` is the genuine local factor; in general `G_p` is not a factor of `F`
at all, but it is exactly what the prime-power coefficients of `-F'/F` see.

---

## 2. Theorem 1 — the local von Mangoldt formula `[PROVED HERE]`

Let `r_1, …, r_e` be the roots of `N_p` (all nonzero, since `N_p(0)=1`) and set the reciprocal-root
power sums `pi_k := sum_j r_j^{-k}`.

> **Theorem 1.** For every `k >= 1`,
>
>   **`b_{p^k} = ( d · [ d | k ] − pi_k ) · log p`.**

*Proof.* `c_{p^k} = [X^k] log G_p = [X^k]( log N_p − log(1 − X^d) )`. Writing
`N_p(X) = prod_j (1 − X/r_j)` (legitimate because `N_p(0)=1`),
`log N_p = − sum_k (pi_k/k) X^k`, while `−log(1−X^d) = sum_{m>=1} X^{dm}/m` contributes `d/k` at
`X^k` exactly when `d | k`. Hence `c_{p^k} = (d[d|k] − pi_k)/k` and `b_{p^k} = k c_{p^k} log p`. ∎

*Consistency.* For `alpha = chi` a Dirichlet character, `N_p(X) = (1 − X^d)/(1 − chi(p)X)`, whose
reciprocal roots are the `d`-th roots of unity other than `chi(p)`; then
`pi_k = d[d|k] − chi(p)^k` and Theorem 1 returns `b_{p^k} = chi(p^k) log p = Lambda(p^k)chi(p^k)`.
For `q = 1` it returns `b_{p^k} = log p = Lambda(p^k)`.

^ exponent(v,j)`.  Ideal multiplicities recover every original exponent, so this
is an injection into ordered `D`-tuples of ideals of the required product norm.  Each monomial has

    (hnonnegative : ∀ x : E, 0 ≤ energy x)

    {H : Type*}
    [AddCommGroup H] [Module ℝ H]
    (S : H →ₗ[ℝ] H)
    (trace : H →ₗ[ℝ] E)
    (A : E →ₗ[ℝ] E)
    (L : Submodule ℝ E)
    (hpositive : ∀ x : E, x ≠ 0 → 0 < inner ℝ (A x) x)
    (hkernel_boundary :

        S x = 0 →

            A.graph ⊓ deningerLinearConormal L)
    (hrelative_unique :
      ∀ x : H, S x = 0 → trace x = 0 → x = 0) :
    LinearMap.ker S = ⊥ := by
  rw [Submodule.eq_bot_iff]
  intro x hx
  have hintersection :

    deningerPositiveCalderonGraph_inf_conormal_eq_bot
      A L hpositive

    hkernel_boundary x hx
  have hpair_zero : (trace x, A (trace x)) = 0 := by
    rw [hintersection] at hpair_mem
    exact hpair_mem
  have htrace : trace x = 0 :=
    congrArg Prod.fst hpair_zero
  exact hrelative_unique x hx htrace

/-!
# Bivariate marginal trace lock

A finite kernel on a product carrier has two canonical coordinate marginals, obtained by tracing
over either factor. Both marginals have exactly the same total trace. The law uses no positivity,
Hermitian symmetry, nondegeneracy, or index bound, so off-diagonal coupling cannot alter it.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-- Jet-coordinate marginal of a finite bivariate kernel. -/
def bivariateJetMarginal
    {P J R : Type*} [Fintype P] [Fintype J] [AddCommMonoid R]
    (C : Matrix (P × J) (P × J) R) : Matrix J J R :=
  fun i j => ∑ p, C (p, i) (p, j)

/-- Source-coordinate marginal of a finite bivariate kernel. -/
def bivariateSourceMarginal
    {P J R : Type*} [Fintype P] [Fintype J] [AddCommMonoid R]
    (C : Matrix (P × J) (P × J) R) : Matrix P P R :=
  fun p q => ∑ i, C (p, i) (q, i)

/-- **Universal bivariate marginal trace lock.** Both coordinate marginals of every finite
bivariate kernel have the same total trace. -/
theorem trace_bivariateJetMarginal_eq_trace_bivariateSourceMarginal
    {P J R : Type*} [Fintype P] [Fintype J] [AddCommMonoid R]
    (C : Matrix (P × J) (P × J) R) :
    Matrix.trace (bivariateJetMarginal C) =
      Matrix.trace (bivariateSourceMarginal C) := by
  change (∑ i : J, ∑ p : P, C (p, i) (p, i)) =
    ∑ p : P, ∑ i : J, C (p, i) (p, i)
  rw [Finset.sum_comm]

end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-!
# The Dirichlet kernel against a Dirichlet polynomial

Pairing with the constant kernel over a symmetric interval,

`∫_{-T}^{T} F(t) dt = ∑_{n < N} a_n ∫_{-T}^{T} n^{it} dt`,

and each inner integral is the Dirichlet kernel `2 sin(T log n)/log n`, of modulus at most
`min(2T, 2/|log n|)`.

The two bounds are what make the pairing selective: near the trivial frequency the kernel is of size
`2T`, and it decays like the reciprocal of the frequency elsewhere.  After a twist by `x^{-it}` the
frequencies become `log(n/x)`, so the pairing localises the coefficient sum to `n ≈ x`.
-/

namespace RHTower.Sieve

open Finset MeasureTheory

/-- The Dirichlet kernel decays in the frequency. -/
theorem norm_integral_exp_phase_symm_le_inv (L : ℝ) (hL : L ≠ 0) (T : ℝ) :
    ‖∫ t in (-T)..T, Complex.exp (((t * L : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)‖ ≤ 2 / |L| := by
  rw [integral_exp_phase_symm L hL T, norm_div, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs]
  have hnum : ‖2 * ((Real.sin (T * L) : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ ≤ 2 := by
    rw [norm_mul, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs]
    have habs : |Real.sin (T * L)| ≤ 1 := Real.abs_sin_le_one _
    have h2 : ‖(2 : ℂ)‖ = 2 := by norm_num
    rw [h2]
    linarith
  have hpos : (0 : ℝ) < |L| := abs_pos.mpr hL
  gcongr

/-- The Dirichlet kernel is bounded by the length of the interval. -/
theorem norm_integral_exp_phase_symm_le_len (L : ℝ) {T : ℝ} (hT : 0 ≤ T) :
    ‖∫ t in (-T)..T, Complex.exp (((t * L : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)‖ ≤ 2 * T := by
  have hbound := intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const
    (f := fun t : ℝ => Complex.exp (((t * L : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I))
    (a := -T) (b := T) (C := 1)
    (fun x _ => le_of_eq (Complex.norm_exp_ofReal_mul_I _))
  have hlen : |T - -T| = 2 * T := by
    rw [show T - -T = 2 * T by ring, abs_of_nonneg (by linarith)]
  rw [hlen, one_mul] at hbound
  exact hbound

/-- **Pairing a Dirichlet polynomial with the Dirichlet kernel.** -/
theorem integral_dirPoly_symm (N : ℕ) (a : Fin N → ℂ) (T : ℝ) :
    (∫ t in (-T)..T, dirPoly N a t)
      = ∑ n : Fin N, a n
          * (∫ t in (-T)..T,
              Complex.exp (((t * Real.log (((n : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1) : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)) := by
  have h := integral_dirPoly_mul N a (K := fun _ : ℝ => (1 : ℂ)) continuous_const (-T) T
  simpa using h

end RHTower.Sieve

/-!
# The Xi Gamma-shape trace is completely monotone on its safe interval

The nonnegative Xi prime-seam trace is a general Dirichlet series with nonnegative coefficients and
nonnegative frequencies.  On its safe shape interval every alternating derivative is the
corresponding nonnegative frequency moment, and the radial Hankel kernel is a Gram kernel of
exponential vectors.

Complete monotonicity is strictly stronger than plain Hankel positivity: the kernel
`K(s,t) = exp (s + t)` is a rank-one Gram kernel, yet the real exponential is not completely
monotone because its generator frequency is negative.
-/

open Complex

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- **Complete monotonicity on the safe shape interval.**  Every alternating derivative of the
global Gamma-shape trace is the corresponding nonnegative frequency moment. -/
theorem xiGammaShapeTrace_completelyMonotone {θ : ℝ} (hθ : 1 < θ) (k : ℕ) :
    ((-1) ^ k * iteratedDeriv k xiGammaShapeTrace ((θ : ℝ) : ℂ)) =
      ((GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.gdMoment
        xiGammaShapeCoefficient xiGammaShapeFrequency θ k : ℝ) : ℂ) := by
  set σ₁ : ℝ := (1 + θ) / 2 with hσ₁
  have hσ₁gt : 1 < σ₁ := by rw [hσ₁]; linarith
  have hh : 0 < θ - σ₁ := by rw [hσ₁]; linarith
  have hsplit : σ₁ + (θ - σ₁) = θ := by ring
  have h := GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.gdSeries_completelyMonotone
    xiGammaShapeCoefficient_nonneg xiGammaShapeFrequency_nonneg
    (summable_xiGammaShapeTwist hσ₁gt) hh k
  rw [hsplit] at h
  exact h

/-- The alternating derivatives are nonnegative reals. -/
theorem xiGammaShapeTrace_alternating_nonneg {θ : ℝ} (hθ : 1 < θ) (k : ℕ) :
    0 ≤ ((-1) ^ k * iteratedDeriv k xiGammaShapeTrace ((θ : ℝ) : ℂ)).re := by
  rw [xiGammaShapeTrace_completelyMonotone hθ k, Complex.ofReal_re]
  exact GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.gdMoment_nonneg
    xiGammaShapeCoefficient_nonneg xiGammaShapeFrequency_nonneg θ k

/-- The real Gamma-shape trace on the safe interval. -/
def xiGammaShapeRealTrace (θ : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.gdRealSeries
    xiGammaShapeCoefficient xiGammaShapeFrequency θ

/-- **Radial Hankel positivity.**  On the safe shape interval the Hankel kernel of the global
Gamma-shape trace is a Gram kernel of exponential vectors, hence positive semidefinite. -/
theorem xiGammaShapeRealTrace_hankel_nonneg {n : ℕ} (θ c : Fin n → ℝ)
    (hθ : ∀ i, 1 < θ i) :
    0 ≤ ∑ i, ∑ j, c i * xiGammaShapeRealTrace (θ i + θ j) * c j := by
  refine GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.gdRealSeries_hankel_nonneg
    xiGammaShapeCoefficient_nonneg xiGammaShapeFrequency_nonneg
    (summable_xiGammaShapeTwist (by norm_num : (1 : ℝ) < 3 / 2)) θ c (fun i => ?_)
  linarith [hθ i]

/-! ## Plain Hankel positivity is strictly weaker -/

/-- The exponential kernel is a rank-one Gram kernel, hence positive semidefinite. -/
theorem exp_hankel_nonneg {n : ℕ} (θ c : Fin n → ℝ) :
    0 ≤ ∑ i, ∑ j, c i * Real.exp (θ i + θ j) * c j := by
  have hkey : ∑ i, ∑ j, c i * Real.exp (θ i + θ j) * c j =
      (∑ i, c i * Real.exp (θ i)) ^ 2 := by
    rw [sq, Finset.sum_mul_sum]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ => ?_
    rw [Real.exp_add]
    ring
  rw [hkey]
  exact sq_nonneg _

/-- The exponential is not completely monotone: its first alternating derivative is negative.
Positive semidefiniteness of the Hankel kernel therefore does not imply complete monotonicity. -/
theorem exp_not_completelyMonotone (θ : ℝ) :
    (-1 : ℝ) ^ 1 * iteratedDeriv 1 Real.exp θ < 0 := by
  have hderiv : iteratedDeriv 1 Real.exp θ = Real.exp θ := by
    rw [iteratedDeriv_one, Real.deriv_exp]
  rw [hderiv]
  simp only [pow_one]
  nlinarith [Real.exp_pos θ]

end

end RHTower

/-!
# The trace quotient isometry

A continuous linear map between Hilbert spaces which is norm preserving on the orthogonal
complement of its kernel induces an isometric isomorphism from the quotient by that kernel.  The
mechanism is the minimality of the orthogonal projection: the quotient norm is the distance to the
kernel, and that distance is attained at the projection, so the quotient norm is the norm of the
component orthogonal to the kernel, which the map preserves.

Together with the orthogonal complementation of the kernel this is the Dirichlet decomposition of
an energy space into its zero-trace part and the orthogonal minimal-energy part carrying the
boundary values.

* `deningerProjection_minimal` : the projection minimizes the distance to the subspace.
* `deningerQuotientNorm_eq` : the quotient norm is the norm of the orthogonal component.
* `deningerZeroTrace_isCompl` : the kernel and its orthogonal complement are complementary.
* `deningerTraceIsometry` : the orthogonal complement of the kernel is isometric to the target.
* `deningerTraceQuotientIsometry` : so is the quotient by the kernel.
-/

namespace RHTower

open scoped InnerProductSpace

section TraceQuotient

variable {E B : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℂ E]
  [NormedAddCommGroup B] [InnerProductSpace ℂ B]

variable (K : Submodule ℂ E) [K.HasOrthogonalProjection]

/-- **The orthogonal projection minimizes the distance to the subspace.**  The residual is
orthogonal to the subspace, so Pythagoras adds a nonnegative square to every other choice. -/
theorem deningerProjection_minimal (x : E) {k : E} (hk : k ∈ K) :
    ‖x - K.starProjection x‖ ≤ ‖x - k‖ := by
  have hmem : K.starProjection x - k ∈ K :=
    K.sub_mem (K.starProjection_apply_mem x) hk
  have horth : ⟪x - K.starProjection x, K.starProjection x - k⟫_ℂ = 0 :=
    Submodule.starProjection_inner_eq_zero (K := K) x _ hmem
  have hsplit : x - k = (x - K.starProjection x) + (K.starProjection x - k) := by
    abel
  have hpy := norm_add_sq_eq_norm_sq_add_norm_sq_of_inner_eq_zero
    (x - K.starProjection x) (K.starProjection x - k) horth
  rw [← hsplit] at hpy
  nlinarith [norm_nonneg (x - k), norm_nonneg (x - K.starProjection x),
    sq_nonneg ‖K.starProjection x - k‖]

/-- **The quotient norm is the norm of the orthogonal component.**  One inequality is the general
bound by any representative, the other is the minimality of the projection applied to
representatives of almost minimal norm. -/
theorem deningerQuotientNorm_eq (x : E) :
    ‖(Submodule.Quotient.mk x : E ⧸ K)‖ = ‖x - K.starProjection x‖ := by
  refine le_antisymm ?_ ?_
  · have hmk : (Submodule.Quotient.mk (x - K.starProjection x) : E ⧸ K)
        = Submodule.Quotient.mk x := by
      refine (Submodule.Quotient.eq K).mpr ?_
      have : x - K.starProjection x - x = -K.starProjection x := by abel
      rw [this]
      exact K.neg_mem (K.starProjection_apply_mem x)
    calc ‖(Submodule.Quotient.mk x : E ⧸ K)‖
        = ‖(Submodule.Quotient.mk (x - K.starProjection x) : E ⧸ K)‖ := by rw [hmk]
      _ ≤ ‖x - K.starProjection x‖ := Submodule.Quotient.norm_mk_le K _
  · refine le_of_forall_pos_le_add fun ε hε => ?_
    obtain ⟨m, hm, hmnorm⟩ :=
      Submodule.Quotient.norm_mk_lt (S := K) (Submodule.Quotient.mk x) hε
    have hmx : m - x ∈ K := (Submodule.Quotient.eq K).mp hm
    have hxm : x - m ∈ K := by
      have : x - m = -(m - x) := by abel
      rw [this]
      exact K.neg_mem hmx
    have hmin := deningerProjection_minimal K x hxm
    have hcancel : x - (x - m) = m := by abel
    rw [hcancel] at hmin
    exact le_of_lt (lt_of_le_of_lt hmin hmnorm)

variable (T : E →L[ℂ] B) [CompleteSpace E]

omit [CompleteSpace E] in
/-- The zero-trace subspace is closed. -/
theorem deningerZeroTrace_isClosed :
    IsClosed ((LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[ℂ] B) : Submodule ℂ E) : Set E) :=
  T.isClosed_ker

instance deningerZeroTrace_completeSpace :
    CompleteSpace (LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[ℂ] B)) :=
  (deningerZeroTrace_isClosed T).completeSpace_coe

/-- **The Dirichlet decomposition.**  The zero-trace subspace and its orthogonal complement are
complementary. -/
theorem deningerZeroTrace_isCompl :
    IsCompl (LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[ℂ] B)) (LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[ℂ] B))ᗮ :=
  Submodule.isCompl_orthogonal _

/-- Every vector splits as a zero-trace vector plus a vector orthogonal to the zero-trace
subspace with the same image. -/
theorem deningerTrace_split (x : E) :
    x - (LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[ℂ] B)).starProjection x
        ∈ (LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[ℂ] B))ᗮ ∧
      T (x - (LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[ℂ] B)).starProjection x) = T x := by
  refine ⟨Submodule.sub_starProjection_mem_orthogonal (K := LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[ℂ] B)) x, ?_⟩
  have hker : (LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[ℂ] B)).starProjection x
      ∈ LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[ℂ] B) :=
    Submodule.starProjection_apply_mem _ x
